tasks.short: Attend one lecture by the supervising instructor.

steps.what: Read the lecture card before this session.
Attend lectures given by the supervising instructor.

tasks.design: Before the lecture, the supervising instructor writes a lecture card with the course, the room, and the one point to watch. The teaching assistant reads that card, then still attends the lecture. If the card has no row, the assistant reads the paper timetable in the same step. The card does not attend the lecture.
tasks.previous_blocker: The room and the one point to watch sat in a paper timetable the assistant had to hunt.
tasks.enabler_now: The supervising instructor writes the course, the room, and the one point on a lecture card before the session.
tasks.still_hard: Attending the lecture and deciding what matters still takes the assistant's presence.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant hears the lecture and chooses what to carry forward.
tasks.altitude: A card shortens the search for the room and the one point. The assistant still attends.

reach.task: Sit in on a course session
reach.learn: A lecture card names the room. It does not attend.

reach.role: English Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
reach.learn: The assistant still attends after reading the card.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the course, the room, and the one point to watch shortens the search when the row is there. The teaching assistant still attends the lecture. Model knowledge.

AI that admits learners, evaluates learning outcomes, or proctors tests is high-risk from 2 December 2027. Attending a lecture is none of that. This paper card is not software. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited annex and the cited date.

assumptions: The supervising instructor writes the lecture card before the session.
Fields are the course, the room, and the one point to watch.
The card does not hold a grade and does not attend the lecture.
If the row is missing, the teaching assistant reads the paper timetable inside s1.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because the supervising instructor keeps the card, counted on the other line.
Works-council consultation for a monitoring or scoring system is out of scope because this design adds none.
Attending the lecture stays in s2 at full time.
unknowns: Whether this desk already keeps a one-line lecture card for each session.
research_questions: How often a first lecture has no row on the lecture card.

incremental.description: No extra assistant upkeep. The supervising instructor keeps the lecture card.
The supervising instructor writes the lecture card: course, room, and one point to watch.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The lecture is the first one, so the lecture card has no row and the assistant reads the paper timetable. The search saving disappears.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange a teaching observation and the later feedback.

steps.what: Read the observer card before this request.
Arrange for supervisors to conduct teaching observations and provide feedback about teaching performance.
Write the agreed observation note after the request.

tasks.design: Before the request, the supervising instructor writes an observer card with the supervisor name, the course, and one open slot. The card does not hold a performance judgement. The teaching assistant reads that card, asks the supervisor, then writes the agreed note by hand. If the card has no row, the assistant reads the paper timetable in the same step. The card does not arrange the observation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The supervisor name and one open slot sat in a paper timetable the assistant had to hunt.
tasks.enabler_now: The supervising instructor writes the supervisor name, the course, and one open slot on an observer card before the request.
tasks.still_hard: Asking the supervisor and writing the agreed note still take the assistant.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant chooses the ask and writes only what was agreed.
tasks.altitude: A card shortens finding the supervisor and the slot. The assistant still arranges the observation and writes the note.

reach.learn: An observer card names a slot. It does not ask the supervisor.

reach.task: Ask for comments on a session
reach.learn: The ask and the later note stay with the person.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the supervisor name, the course, and one open slot shortens the search when the row is there. The teaching assistant still arranges the observation and writes the note. The card does not hold a performance judgement. Model knowledge.

The exam board appoints the examiners who set results. Arranging an observation is not the examiner setting a result, and this assistant does not set a result. This paper card is not software. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited statute.

assumptions: The supervising instructor writes the observer card before the request.
Fields are the supervisor name, the course, and one open slot.
The card does not hold a performance judgement and does not arrange the observation.
s3 writes the agreed note from the spoken request in s2.
If the row is missing, the teaching assistant reads the paper timetable inside s1.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because the supervising instructor keeps the card, counted on the other line.
Works-council consultation for a monitoring or scoring system is out of scope because this design adds none.
Arranging the observation stays in s2 at full time, and writing the note stays in s3 at full time.
unknowns: Whether this desk already keeps a one-line observer card for each course.
research_questions: How often a new course has no row on the observer card.

incremental.description: No extra assistant upkeep. The supervising instructor keeps the observer card.
The supervising instructor writes the observer card: supervisor name, course, and one open slot.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The course is new, so the observer card has no row and the assistant reads the paper timetable. The search saving disappears.

tasks.short: Assist faculty at one student conference.

steps.what: Read the conference card before this meeting.
Assist faculty members or staff with student conferences.

tasks.design: Before the conference, the faculty member writes a conference card with the course, the time, and one topic title. The card does not hold the private matter. The teaching assistant reads that card, then still assists at the conference. If the card has no row, the assistant reads the paper list in the same step. The card does not sit in the conference.
tasks.previous_blocker: The course, the time, and the topic title sat in a paper list the assistant had to hunt.
tasks.enabler_now: The faculty member writes the course, the time, and one topic title on a conference card before the meeting.
tasks.still_hard: Assisting at the conference still takes the assistant in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant hears the conference and helps the faculty member there.
tasks.altitude: A card shortens finding the time and the topic title. The assistant still assists.

reach.task: Sit in on a student meeting
reach.learn: A conference card names a topic title. It does not hold the private matter.
The assistant still assists in the room.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the course, the time, and one topic title shortens the search when the row is there. The teaching assistant still assists at the conference. The card does not hold the private matter. Model knowledge.

Kennisnet says no personal data in AI tools. This design adds no AI tool, so the conference stays in the room and no personal data goes into an AI tool. This paper card is not software. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited guidance.
